concepts.title: Place Value & Large Numbers
concepts.summary: Read, write, and compare multi-digit numbers up to crores using Indian and International place value systems.

quiz.prompt: How many lakhs make one crore in the Indian place value system?
quiz.explanation: One crore equals 1,00,00,000 which is 100 × 1,00,000 (100 lakhs).

quiz.prompt: What is the place value of 7 in 4,72,810?
quiz.explanation: 7 sits in the ten-thousands place, so its place value is 70,000.

concepts.title: Factors, Multiples & Primes
concepts.summary: Identify prime and composite numbers, factor trees, HCF, and LCM using divisibility rules.
concepts.formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b

quiz.prompt: Which is the smallest even prime number?
quiz.explanation: 2 has exactly two distinct factors (1 and 2), making it the only even prime.

quiz.prompt: What is the LCM of 6 and 8?
quiz.explanation: Multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24... and 24 is the smallest multiple divisible by 6.

concepts.title: Equivalent Fractions & Operations
concepts.summary: Represent parts of a whole, simplify equivalent fractions, and add or subtract unlike fractions.

quiz.prompt: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
quiz.explanation: Multiplying numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 3 gives 9/12.

quiz.prompt: What is 1/3 + 1/6?

concepts.title: Decimals & Metric Conversions
concepts.summary: Convert tenths and hundredths between fractions and decimals and apply them to length, mass, and currency.

quiz.prompt: Express 3/10 + 7/100 as a decimal.
quiz.explanation: 3 tenths and 7 hundredths combine to 0.37.

quiz.prompt: How many meters are in 2.45 km?

concepts.title: Angles, Triangles & Symmetry
concepts.summary: Measure acute, right, and obtuse angles with a protractor and explore line symmetry in polygons.

quiz.prompt: An angle measuring 135° is classified as:
quiz.explanation: Any angle strictly between 90° and 180° is an obtuse angle.

quiz.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
quiz.explanation: All three medians/altitudes of an equilateral triangle are lines of symmetry.

concepts.title: Perimeter & Area of Rectangles
concepts.summary: Calculate boundary lengths and unit-square areas for squares, rectangles, and composite grids.

quiz.prompt: Find the area of a rectangle with length 12 cm and breadth 5 cm.
quiz.explanation: Area = length × breadth = 12 × 5 = 60 cm².

quiz.prompt: What is the perimeter of a square whose area is 49 cm²?
quiz.explanation: Side = √49 = 7 cm, so perimeter = 4 × 7 = 28 cm.

concepts.title: Seed Dispersal & Plant Growth
concepts.summary: Explore seed anatomy, germination conditions, and wind/water/animal dispersal mechanisms.

quiz.prompt: Which three conditions are essential for seed germination?
quiz.explanation: Seeds require moisture, suitable temperature, and oxygen to activate embryo growth.

quiz.prompt: Dandelion seeds have hair-like structures suited for dispersal by:
quiz.explanation: Lightweight feathery pappus hairs allow wind currents to carry dandelion seeds.

concepts.title: Skeletal & Nervous Systems
concepts.summary: Understand joints, voluntary/involuntary muscles, and how the brain, spinal cord, and nerves coordinate.

quiz.prompt: Which type of joint allows movement in all directions, such as in the shoulder?
quiz.explanation: A ball-and-socket joint permits multi-axial rotational movement.

quiz.prompt: Reflex actions are primarily controlled by the:
quiz.explanation: The spinal cord triggers rapid involuntary reflex arcs before conscious brain processing.

concepts.title: States of Matter & Physical Changes
concepts.summary: Compare particle spacing in solids, liquids, and gases, and identify reversible vs. irreversible changes.

quiz.prompt: In which state of matter are molecules most tightly packed in fixed positions?
quiz.explanation: Solids have strong intermolecular forces holding particles in fixed lattices.

quiz.prompt: Melting of ice into liquid water is an example of a:
quiz.explanation: No new substance forms and freezing reverses the state back to ice.

concepts.title: Force, Work & Simple Machines
concepts.summary: Classify levers, pulleys, inclined planes, and wedges that multiply force or change force direction.

quiz.prompt: A pair of scissors is an example of which class of lever?
quiz.explanation: In scissors, the fulcrum lies between the effort and the load (Class 1).

quiz.prompt: Which simple machine wraps an inclined plane around a central cylinder?
quiz.explanation: A screw consists of a helical inclined plane wrapped around a shaft.

concepts.title: Earth, Moon Phases & Eclipses
concepts.summary: Model lunar phases, solar vs. lunar eclipses, and artificial satellite orbits.

quiz.prompt: A solar eclipse occurs when the:
options: Earth comes between Sun and Moon
Moon comes between Sun and Earth
Sun comes between Earth and Moon
Earth tilts away from the Sun
quiz.explanation: The Moon casts its shadow onto Earth when positioned directly between Sun and Earth.

quiz.prompt: What causes tides in Earth’s oceans?
options: Gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun
quiz.explanation: Differential gravitational attraction from the Moon (and Sun) creates tidal bulges.

concepts.title: Integers & Directed Numbers
concepts.summary: Represent positive and negative integers on a number line and perform integer addition and subtraction.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate (-8) + (+13).
quiz.explanation: Moving 13 units right from -8 lands on +5.

quiz.prompt: Which integer is greater: -15 or -4?
quiz.explanation: -4 lies to the right of -15 on the number line.

concepts.title: Ratio, Proportion & Unitary Method
concepts.summary: Compare quantities using simplified ratios, verify proportionality, and solve unitary rate problems.
concepts.formula: a : b :: c : d  ⇒  a × d = b × c

quiz.prompt: Simplify the ratio 24 : 36.
quiz.explanation: Dividing both terms by their HCF (12) yields 2 : 3.

quiz.prompt: If 5 notebooks cost ₹125, what is the cost of 8 notebooks?
quiz.explanation: Cost of 1 notebook = ₹25, so 8 notebooks cost 8 × 25 = ₹200.

concepts.title: Introduction to Algebra & Variables
concepts.summary: Translate word statements into algebraic expressions with variables, constants, and simple equations.

quiz.prompt: Write an expression for "5 subtracted from twice a number x".
quiz.explanation: Twice x is 2x, and subtracting 5 gives 2x - 5.

quiz.prompt: Solve for m: 3m = 27.
quiz.explanation: Dividing both sides by 3 gives m = 9.

concepts.title: Basic Geometrical Ideas & Polygons
concepts.summary: Distinguish rays, line segments, intersecting/parallel lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles.

quiz.prompt: A line segment connecting two points on a circle passing through the center is a:
quiz.explanation: The longest chord passing through the center of a circle is its diameter.

quiz.prompt: How many vertices does a pentagon have?
quiz.explanation: A pentagon is a 5-sided polygon with 5 vertices.

concepts.title: Mensuration of Composite Shapes
concepts.summary: Decompose L-shaped figures into rectangles to determine total perimeter and area.
concepts.formula: Perimeter of regular n-gon = n × side

quiz.prompt: Find the perimeter of a regular hexagon with side 7.5 cm.
quiz.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides: 6 × 7.5 = 45 cm.

quiz.prompt: A square floor of side 4 m is covered by tiles of area 0.5 m². How many tiles are needed?
quiz.explanation: Floor area = 16 m²; 16 / 0.5 = 32 tiles.

concepts.title: Data Handling & Bar Graphs
concepts.summary: Organize raw observations with tally marks and interpret pictographs and scaled bar graphs.
concepts.formula: Scale = Units per 1 cm bar height

quiz.prompt: If 1 symbol represents 15 books, how many symbols represent 90 books?
quiz.explanation: 90 ÷ 15 = 6 symbols.

quiz.prompt: Tally marks grouped in bundles with a diagonal slash represent how many counts?
quiz.explanation: Four vertical bars crossed by one diagonal slash represent 5.

concepts.title: Components of Food & Balanced Diet
concepts.summary: Test for starch, proteins, and fats and connect vitamin/mineral deficiencies to disorders.

quiz.prompt: Which chemical turns blue-black in the presence of starch?
quiz.explanation: Dilute iodine binds with amylose in starch to produce a blue-black complex.

quiz.prompt: Deficiency of Vitamin C leads to:
quiz.explanation: Lack of Vitamin C impairs collagen synthesis, causing bleeding gums (scurvy).

concepts.title: Separation of Mixtures
concepts.summary: Select filtration, sedimentation, decantation, evaporation, and magnetic separation for mixtures.

quiz.prompt: Which method separates dissolved common salt from seawater?
quiz.explanation: Water vaporizes on heating while salt crystals remain behind.

quiz.prompt: Threshing followed by winnowing separates husk from grain based on difference in:
quiz.explanation: Wind carries lighter chaff away while heavier grains fall vertically.

concepts.title: Measurement & Types of Motion
concepts.summary: Measure lengths in SI units and distinguish rectilinear, circular, and periodic motion.

quiz.prompt: The swinging of a pendulum is an example of:
quiz.explanation: A pendulum repeats its to-and-fro path in fixed time intervals.

quiz.prompt: What is the SI unit of length?
quiz.explanation: The meter (m) is the standard base SI unit for length.

concepts.title: Light, Shadows & Reflections
concepts.summary: Investigate rectilinear propagation of light through pinhole cameras, shadows, and plane mirrors.

quiz.prompt: The image formed inside a pinhole camera is always:
quiz.explanation: Light rays cross straight through the aperture, producing an upside-down image.

quiz.prompt: Materials that allow light to pass partially through them are called:
quiz.explanation: Translucent materials scatter part of the incident light (e.g., frosted glass).

quiz.prompt: Which material acts as an electrical insulator?
quiz.explanation: Dry rubber lacks free charge carriers and blocks electric current.

quiz.prompt: Like poles of two bar magnets always:
quiz.explanation: North repels North and South repels South.

concepts.summary: Classify numbers in p/q form, locate them on the number line, and compute sums and products.

quiz.prompt: What is the additive inverse of -5/9?
quiz.explanation: -5/9 + 5/9 = 0, so 5/9 is the additive inverse.

concepts.title: Exponents, Powers & Scientific Notation
concepts.summary: Apply laws of exponents for multiplication, division, and power of a power.

quiz.prompt: Simplify 2³ × 2⁴.
quiz.explanation: When bases match, add exponents: 3 + 4 = 7, giving 2⁷.

quiz.prompt: What is the value of 7⁰ + 5⁰?
quiz.explanation: Any non-zero base to the power 0 equals 1, so 1 + 1 = 2.

concepts.title: Simple Linear Equations
concepts.summary: Balance equations using transposition and solve multi-step word problems.

quiz.prompt: Solve: 4x - 7 = 21.
If 3(y + 2) = 24, find y.
quiz.explanation: y + 2 = 8, hence y = 6.

concepts.title: Lines, Angles & Triangle Properties
concepts.summary: Prove angle-sum and exterior-angle theorems and verify triangle inequality and congruence rules.

quiz.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are 45° and 65°. What is the third angle?
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its:
quiz.explanation: By the exterior angle theorem, it equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.

concepts.title: Percentages, Profit & Simple Interest
concepts.summary: Compute percentage change, profit/loss percent, and simple interest over time.

quiz.prompt: Find the simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
An item bought for ₹400 is sold for ₹460. What is the profit percentage?

concepts.title: Congruence & Area of Circles
concepts.summary: Apply SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS congruence criteria and compute circumference and area of circles.

quiz.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm (use π = 22/7).
Which criterion proves two right-angled triangles congruent using hypotenuse and one leg?
quiz.explanation: RHS stands for Right angle – Hypotenuse – Side.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis & Digestive Systems
concepts.summary: Trace chlorophyll-driven glucose synthesis and human enzymatic digestion across organs.

quiz.prompt: Which gas is absorbed from air through stomata for photosynthesis?
quiz.explanation: Leaves take in CO₂ through stomatal pores to synthesize carbohydrates.

quiz.prompt: Bile juice produced by the liver helps digest:
quiz.explanation: Bile emulsifies large fat globules into smaller droplets for lipase action.

concepts.title: Heat, Temperature & Transfer Modes
concepts.summary: Contrast clinical vs. laboratory thermometers and conduction, convection, and radiation.

quiz.prompt: Heat from the Sun reaches Earth primarily through:
quiz.explanation: Radiation requires no material medium and travels across the vacuum of space.

quiz.prompt: Sea breeze during daytime is driven by:
quiz.explanation: Warm air rises over land and cooler air from the sea flows inward by convection.

concepts.title: Acids, Bases & Neutralisation
concepts.summary: Use litmus, turmeric, and phenolphthalein indicators and write word equations for neutralisation.

quiz.prompt: A basic solution turns red litmus paper:
quiz.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red.

quiz.prompt: Which compound relieves ant-sting irritation caused by formic acid?
quiz.explanation: Mildly basic calamine neutralizes the injected formic acid.

concepts.title: Respiration & Transportation in Organisms
concepts.summary: Compare aerobic vs. anaerobic respiration and trace blood flow and plant xylem/phloem transport.

quiz.prompt: Which vascular tissue carries water and dissolved minerals upward from roots?
quiz.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and minerals from roots to leaves.

quiz.prompt: Which blood cells transport oxygen bound to hemoglobin?
quiz.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin which binds oxygen.

quiz.prompt: A car travels 180 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in m/s?

quiz.explanation: Convex mirrors always form erect, diminished images over a wide field.

quiz.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are 45° and 65°. What is the third angle?
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its:
quiz.explanation: By the exterior angle theorem, it equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.

concepts.title: Percentages, Profit & Simple Interest
concepts.summary: Compute percentage change, profit/loss percent, and simple interest over time.

quiz.prompt: Find the simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
An item bought for ₹400 is sold for ₹460. What is the profit percentage?

concepts.title: Congruence & Area of Circles
concepts.summary: Apply SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS congruence criteria and compute circumference and area of circles.

quiz.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm (use π = 22/7).
Which criterion proves two right-angled triangles congruent using hypotenuse and one leg?
quiz.explanation: RHS stands for Right angle – Hypotenuse – Side.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis & Digestive Systems
concepts.summary: Trace chlorophyll-driven glucose synthesis and human enzymatic digestion across organs.

quiz.prompt: Which gas is absorbed from air through stomata for photosynthesis?
quiz.explanation: Leaves take in CO₂ through stomatal pores to synthesize carbohydrates.

quiz.prompt: Bile juice produced by the liver helps digest:
quiz.explanation: Bile emulsifies large fat globules into smaller droplets for lipase action.

concepts.title: Heat, Temperature & Transfer Modes
concepts.summary: Contrast clinical vs. laboratory thermometers and conduction, convection, and radiation.

quiz.prompt: Heat from the Sun reaches Earth primarily through:
quiz.explanation: Radiation requires no material medium and travels across the vacuum of space.

quiz.prompt: Sea breeze during daytime is driven by:
quiz.explanation: Warm air rises over land and cooler air from the sea flows inward by convection.

concepts.title: Acids, Bases & Neutralisation
concepts.summary: Use litmus, turmeric, and phenolphthalein indicators and write word equations for neutralisation.

quiz.prompt: A basic solution turns red litmus paper:
quiz.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red.

quiz.prompt: Which compound relieves ant-sting irritation caused by formic acid?
quiz.explanation: Mildly basic calamine neutralizes the injected formic acid.

concepts.title: Respiration & Transportation in Organisms
concepts.summary: Compare aerobic vs. anaerobic respiration and trace blood flow and plant xylem/phloem transport.

quiz.prompt: Which vascular tissue carries water and dissolved minerals upward from roots?
quiz.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and minerals from roots to leaves.

quiz.prompt: Which blood cells transport oxygen bound to hemoglobin?
quiz.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin which binds oxygen.

concepts.title: Speed-Time Graphs & Spherical Mirrors
concepts.summary: Calculate average speed from distance-time graphs and examine concave/convex mirror images.

quiz.prompt: A car travels 180 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in m/s?
Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles for a wider field of view?
quiz.explanation: Convex mirrors always form erect, diminished images over a wide field.

concepts.title: Squares, Cubes & Radicals
concepts.summary: Determine square roots and cube roots via prime factorization and estimation.

quiz.prompt: What is the square root of 1,225?
What is the cube root of 512?

concepts.title: Algebraic Expressions & Identities
concepts.summary: Multiply polynomials and apply standard binomial identities to simplify expressions.

quiz.prompt: Expand (x - 4)².
quiz.explanation: Using (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b², we get x² - 8x + 16.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 98 × 102 using an algebraic identity.

concepts.title: Linear Equations in One Variable
concepts.summary: Solve equations with variables on both sides and reduce fractional linear equations.
concepts.formula: ax + b = cx + d  ⇒  x = (d - b)/(a - c)

quiz.prompt: Solve for x: 5x - 3 = 2x + 12.
quiz.explanation: 3x = 15, therefore x = 5.

quiz.prompt: If (x/2) + (x/3) = 10, what is x?

concepts.title: Factorisation of Polynomials
concepts.summary: Factor quadratic trinomials by splitting the middle term and applying difference of squares.

quiz.prompt: Factorise x² - 9x + 20.
quiz.explanation: -4 and -5 sum to -9 and multiply to +20.

quiz.prompt: Factorise 49p² - 36.

concepts.title: Compound Interest & Discounts
concepts.summary: Calculate marked price discounts, GST, and compound interest compounded annually or half-yearly.

quiz.prompt: Find the amount on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% p.a. compounded annually.
An article marked at ₹800 is sold at a 15% discount. What is the selling price?

concepts.title: Surface Area & Volume of Solids
concepts.summary: Compute lateral and total surface areas and volumes of cubes, cuboids, and right circular cylinders.

quiz.prompt: What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (π = 22/7)?
Find the total surface area of a cube of edge 5 cm.
quiz.explanation: TSA of a cube = 6a² = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

concepts.title: Cell Structure & Microorganisms
concepts.summary: Compare plant and animal cell organelles and understand beneficial vs. pathogenic microbes.

quiz.prompt: Which organelle is present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
quiz.explanation: Plant cells have rigid cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

quiz.prompt: Which bacterium converts milk into curd?
quiz.explanation: Lactobacillus multiplies in milk and converts lactose into lactic acid.

concepts.title: Metals, Non-Metals & Combustion
concepts.summary: Contrast malleability and reactivity of metals with flame zones and ignition temperature.

quiz.prompt: Which non-metal is liquid at room temperature?
quiz.explanation: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature (mercury is a metal).

quiz.prompt: Which zone of a candle flame is the hottest?
quiz.explanation: Complete combustion occurs in the outermost blue zone, reaching maximum temperature.

concepts.title: Force, Pressure & Friction
concepts.summary: Analyze contact/non-contact forces, fluid and atmospheric pressure, and rolling vs. sliding friction.

quiz.prompt: Why do school bags have wide shoulder straps?
options: To increase area and reduce pressure on shoulders
quiz.explanation: Larger contact area distributes force, reducing pressure (P = F/A).

quiz.prompt: Which type of friction is the smallest for a given pair of surfaces?
quiz.explanation: Rolling motion minimizes surface interlocking, making rolling friction lowest.

concepts.title: Sound, Frequency & Amplitude
concepts.summary: Relate pitch to frequency, loudness to amplitude, and trace human ear vibration transmission.

quiz.prompt: What is the audible frequency range for the human ear?
quiz.explanation: Humans detect sound waves between 20 Hz and 20 kHz.

quiz.prompt: Loudness of a sound depends directly on its:
quiz.explanation: Loudness is proportional to the square of vibration amplitude.

concepts.title: Chemical Effects of Current & Refraction
concepts.summary: Examine electroplating, laws of reflection, multiple mirror images, and human eye anatomy.

quiz.prompt: If the angle between an incident ray and a plane mirror is 35°, what is the angle of reflection?
quiz.explanation: Angle of incidence from the normal is 90° - 35° = 55°, so angle of reflection = 55°.

quiz.prompt: In electroplating copper onto an iron spoon, the spoon is connected to the:
quiz.explanation: Positive copper ions migrate toward and deposit on the negative cathode.

concepts.title: Real Numbers & Surds
concepts.summary: Explore irrational numbers, decimal expansions, and rationalizing denominators of surds.

quiz.prompt: Which of the following is an irrational number?
quiz.explanation: 7 is not a perfect square, so √7 has a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal expansion.

quiz.prompt: Rationalize the denominator of 1 / √5.
quiz.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by √5 to get √5 / 5.

concepts.title: Polynomials & Remainder Theorem
concepts.summary: Find zeros of polynomials, apply Remainder and Factor theorems, and factor cubic expressions.
concepts.formula: If p(a) = 0, then (x - a) is a factor of p(x)

quiz.prompt: What is the remainder when x³ + 3x² + 3x + 1 is divided by (x + 1)?
quiz.explanation: By Remainder Theorem, p(-1) = (-1)³ + 3(-1)² + 3(-1) + 1 = 0.

quiz.prompt: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x⁴ - 3x² + 9?
quiz.explanation: The highest power of the variable x with non-zero coefficient is 4.

concepts.title: Cartesian Plane & Linear Equations in 2 Variables
concepts.summary: Plot points across four quadrants and graph linear equations ax + by + c = 0.

quiz.prompt: In which quadrant does the point (-4, 6) lie?
quiz.explanation: Negative x and positive y place the point in Quadrant II.

quiz.prompt: Which point lies on the line 2x + y = 7?
quiz.explanation: 2(2) + 3 = 7, which satisfies the equation.

concepts.title: Triangles, Quadrilaterals & Circle Theorems
concepts.summary: Apply midpoint theorem, equal chords subtending equal angles, and cyclic quadrilateral properties.
concepts.formula: Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°

quiz.prompt: If one angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 72°, what is its opposite angle?
quiz.explanation: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: 180° - 72° = 108°.

quiz.prompt: The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle is:
quiz.explanation: Angle in a semicircle is always a right angle (90°).

concepts.title: Heron's Formula, Cones & Spheres
concepts.summary: Compute triangle area from three sides and find surface areas and volumes of cones and spheres.

quiz.prompt: Find the area of a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm.
What is the surface area of a sphere of radius r?
quiz.explanation: The curved/total surface area of a sphere is 4πr².

concepts.title: Histograms & Empirical Probability
concepts.summary: Construct frequency polygons and compute experimental probabilities from grouped datasets.

quiz.prompt: A coin is tossed 200 times and heads appears 112 times. What is P(Heads)?
For a histogram with unequal class widths, bar height is proportional to:
quiz.explanation: Adjusted frequency (frequency density) keeps bar areas proportional to frequencies.

concepts.title: Atoms, Molecules & Mole Concept
concepts.summary: Apply laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions, write chemical formulas, and compute moles.

quiz.prompt: How many moles are present in 36 g of water (H₂O, molar mass = 18 g/mol)?
quiz.explanation: n = 36 / 18 = 2 moles.

quiz.prompt: What is the chemical formula of aluminium oxide (Al³⁺ and O²⁻)?
quiz.explanation: Crossing valencies 3 and 2 yields Al₂O₃.

concepts.title: Structure of the Atom & Valency
concepts.summary: Compare Bohr energy shells, isotopes, isobars, and calculate valency from electronic configuration.

quiz.prompt: What is the maximum number of electrons in the M shell (n = 3)?
quiz.explanation: 2n² = 2 × 3² = 18 electrons.

quiz.prompt: Isotopes of an element always have the same:
quiz.explanation: Isotopes share the same number of protons (atomic number) but differ in neutrons.

concepts.title: Equations of Motion & Newton’s Laws
concepts.summary: Derive the three kinematic equations graphically and apply inertia, F = ma, and momentum conservation.
concepts.formula: v = u + at,  s = ut + ½at²,  F = ma

quiz.prompt: A body starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 5 s. Find its final velocity.
What is the SI unit of linear momentum?
quiz.explanation: Momentum p = m × v, measured in kg·m/s.

concepts.title: Gravitation, Work & Mechanical Energy
concepts.summary: Use universal gravitation, Archimedes’ buoyancy principle, kinetic/potential energy, and power.

quiz.prompt: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force becomes:
quiz.explanation: Gravitational force is inversely proportional to r², so (1/2)² = 1/4.

quiz.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 4 kg object moving at 5 m/s.

concepts.summary: Differentiate prokaryotic vs. eukaryotic cells, mitosis/meiosis, and meristematic vs. permanent tissues.

quiz.prompt: Which organelle synthesizes ATP and is termed the powerhouse of the cell?
quiz.explanation: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration to produce ATP.

quiz.prompt: Which plant tissue provides flexibility to young stems without breaking?
quiz.explanation: Collenchyma cells have corner-thickened living walls conferring mechanical flexibility.

concepts.title: Quadratic Equations & Discriminant
concepts.summary: Solve ax² + bx + c = 0 by factoring and the quadratic formula, and classify roots via D = b² - 4ac.

quiz.prompt: When does a quadratic equation have two equal real roots?
quiz.explanation: When discriminant b² - 4ac = 0, both roots collapse to -b / 2a.

quiz.prompt: Find the roots of x² - 7x + 12 = 0.
quiz.explanation: (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0 gives roots x = 3 and x = 4.

concepts.summary: Derive the nth term and sum of first n terms of sequences with constant common difference.

quiz.prompt: Find the 10th term of the AP: 2, 7, 12, ...

concepts.summary: Calculate Euclidean distances between points and coordinates dividing a segment in ratio m₁:m₂.

quiz.prompt: Find the distance between (0, 0) and (6, 8).
What is the midpoint of the segment joining (-2, 5) and (6, -1)?

concepts.title: Trigonometric Ratios & Identities
concepts.summary: Relate right-triangle ratios (sin, cos, tan), standard angles, and Pythagorean trigonometric identities.

quiz.prompt: If sin A = 3/5 (A acute), what is cos A?
Evaluate sin 30° + cos 60°.
quiz.explanation: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so their sum is 1.

concepts.title: Grouped Mean, Median & Classical Probability
concepts.summary: Compute mean, median, and mode of grouped frequency distributions and exact probability events.
concepts.formula: Mode = l + [(f₁ - f₀)/(2f₁ - f₀ - f₂)] × h

quiz.prompt: Two fair dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum of 7?
quiz.explanation: 6 favorable pairs out of 36 outcomes give a sum of 7: 6/36 = 1/6.

quiz.prompt: Which empirical relationship links Mean, Median, and Mode?
quiz.explanation: The empirical relation is 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.

concepts.title: Chemical Reactions, Acids & Salts
concepts.summary: Balance redox, displacement, and double-displacement equations and understand pH scale reactions.

quiz.prompt: When zinc reacts with dilute H₂SO₄, which gas is evolved?
quiz.explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑.

quiz.prompt: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
quiz.explanation: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄ · ½H₂O) is Plaster of Paris.

concepts.title: Carbon Compounds & Functional Groups
concepts.summary: Name homologous series (alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids) and analyze esterification.

quiz.prompt: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of ethane (C₂H₆)?
quiz.explanation: One C–C single bond plus six C–H single bonds gives 7 covalent bonds.

quiz.prompt: Which functional group characterizes carboxylic acids?
quiz.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group.

concepts.title: Life Processes, Control & Heredity
concepts.summary: Map nephron filtration, reflex arcs, hormone regulation, and Mendelian monohybrid/dihybrid crosses.

quiz.prompt: What is the structural and functional filtration unit of the human kidney?
quiz.explanation: Nephrons filter blood plasma and reabsorb water/nutrients to form urine.

quiz.prompt: In Mendel’s monohybrid cross (Tt × Tt), what fraction of offspring are short (tt)?
quiz.explanation: Genotypes are 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 1/4 are recessive short.

concepts.title: Refraction, Lenses & Human Eye
concepts.summary: Apply lens formula, magnification, Snell’s law, and myopia/hypermetropia corrective lenses.

quiz.prompt: What is the power of a convex lens with focal length +25 cm?
quiz.explanation: P = 1 / 0.25 m = +4 Dioptres.

quiz.prompt: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected using a:
quiz.explanation: A diverging concave lens shifts the focal point back onto the retina.

quiz.prompt: Two 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel have an equivalent resistance of:

quiz.prompt: Two fair dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum of 7?
quiz.explanation: 6 favorable pairs out of 36 outcomes give a sum of 7: 6/36 = 1/6.

quiz.prompt: Which empirical relationship links Mean, Median, and Mode?
quiz.explanation: The empirical relation is 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.

concepts.title: Chemical Reactions, Acids & Salts
concepts.summary: Balance redox, displacement, and double-displacement equations and understand pH scale reactions.

quiz.prompt: When zinc reacts with dilute H₂SO₄, which gas is evolved?
quiz.explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑.

quiz.prompt: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
quiz.explanation: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄ · ½H₂O) is Plaster of Paris.

concepts.title: Carbon Compounds & Functional Groups
concepts.summary: Name homologous series (alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids) and analyze esterification.

quiz.prompt: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of ethane (C₂H₆)?
quiz.explanation: One C–C single bond plus six C–H single bonds gives 7 covalent bonds.

quiz.prompt: Which functional group characterizes carboxylic acids?
quiz.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group.

concepts.title: Life Processes, Control & Heredity
concepts.summary: Map nephron filtration, reflex arcs, hormone regulation, and Mendelian monohybrid/dihybrid crosses.

quiz.prompt: What is the structural and functional filtration unit of the human kidney?
quiz.explanation: Nephrons filter blood plasma and reabsorb water/nutrients to form urine.

quiz.prompt: In Mendel’s monohybrid cross (Tt × Tt), what fraction of offspring are short (tt)?
quiz.explanation: Genotypes are 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 1/4 are recessive short.

concepts.title: Refraction, Lenses & Human Eye
concepts.summary: Apply lens formula, magnification, Snell’s law, and myopia/hypermetropia corrective lenses.

quiz.prompt: What is the power of a convex lens with focal length +25 cm?
quiz.explanation: P = 1 / 0.25 m = +4 Dioptres.

quiz.prompt: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected using a:
quiz.explanation: A diverging concave lens shifts the focal point back onto the retina.

concepts.title: Ohm’s Law, Circuits & Electromagnetism
concepts.summary: Compute series/parallel equivalent resistance, Joule heating, and Fleming’s left/right-hand rules.

quiz.prompt: Two 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel have an equivalent resistance of:
How much charge flows through a wire carrying 2 A current for 30 seconds?
quiz.explanation: Q = I × t = 2 × 30 = 60 Coulombs.
